newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps -Down on API, shrugs Deng news.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps -Down on API, shrugs Deng news.

text.p: Singapore oil product swaps were down slightly at midday on Thursday following bearish American Petroleum Institute (API) stock report leading to weaker crude and heating oil prices, traders said.
"The market was down because of API and crude," one broker said.
March gas oil swaps were last quoted at $25.55/$25.70 per barrel, down from Wednesday's $25.70/$25.80. It traded earlier in the day at $25.80 and $25.70 per barrel, brokers said.
Front month NYMEX heating oil last traded down 0.59 cents per gallon to 59 cents on the after-hours ACCESS system while WTI was down 22 cents per barrel to $22.57.
The weaker market were due to the release of API statistics which revealed a 3.12 million build in crude stocks to 304.88 million barrels.
Brokers said the market did not react to news of Deng Xiaoping's death but added that some players used it to talk the market down or up.
"Those who were long said the death will lead to an increase of gasoil during the funeral and those who were short said demand will drop as factories close down," one broker said.
One Chinese source said the death is not likely to have any immediate impact on the oil market as China's oil import/export policy is not expected to change.
He said China is not likely to buy large amounts of gas oil or fuel oil as stocks at local refineries were high.
Fuel oil swaps also edged down in part also due to the reduced buying interest from China.
March swaps were last quoted at $102.25/$103.25, down about 50 cents from Wednesday.
